title: Cut, replace and change parts of file names in a bash script
summary: Shows the bash shortcuts for working with text: remove the extension, read the extension, replace spaces, change upper and lower case. The script only prints the results and renames nothing.

steps.explain: Save the script. Create the file with nano and paste the whole text, including the first line that starts with #!. Press Ctrl+O then Enter to save, and Ctrl+X to exit.
steps.expect: An empty editor opens. After you save, the file exists in the current folder.

steps.explain: Check the script for syntax mistakes without running it.
steps.expect: No output means the syntax is correct.

steps.explain: Make the script executable so you can start it by its name.
steps.expect: No output. ls -l then shows x in the permissions.

steps.explain: Run the script on three names: one with spaces and a capital extension, one plain file, and one with no extension.
steps.cmd: ./<FILE> 'My Holiday Photo.JPG' notes.txt README; echo exit code $?
steps.expect: without extension: My Holiday Photo, no spaces: My_Holiday_Photo.JPG, extension upper: notes.TXT, .txt changed to .md: notes.md, extension: (none) for README, then exit code 0

warnings: ${name%.*} works only on the text you give it. It does not check that the file exists on disk.
A name that starts with a dot, such as .bashrc, loses its name part with ${name%.*}. Check for that case if your names can start with a dot.
${var/a/b} replaces only the first match, while ${var//a/b} replaces every match. Use the double slash for spaces.

script.content:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# rename-tidy.sh - shows bash string tricks on file names. It only prints; nothing is renamed.
# Usage: ./rename-tidy.sh FILE [FILE...]

set -euo pipefail

if (( $# == 0 )); then
    echo "usage: $0 FILE [FILE...]" >&2
    exit 2
fi

for path in "$@"; do
    name=${path##*/}              # remove the folder part: keep what follows the last /
    stem=${name%.*}               # remove the shortest ".something" at the end
    ext=""
    if [[ $name == *.* ]]; then
        ext=${name##*.}           # keep only what follows the last dot
    fi
    no_spaces=${name// /_}        # ${var//a/b}: replace EVERY space with _
    new_name=${name/%.txt/.md}    # ${var/%a/b}: replace .txt only at the END of the name
    shouting=$stem
    if [[ -n $ext ]]; then
        shouting=$stem.${ext^^}   # ${var^^}: upper case (bash 4 or newer)
    fi

    echo "== $path"
    printf '  name without folder: %s\n' "$name"
    printf '  without extension:   %s\n' "$stem"
    printf '  extension:           %s\n' "${ext:-(none)}"
    printf '  no spaces:           %s\n' "$no_spaces"
    printf '  extension upper:     %s\n' "$shouting"
    printf '  .txt changed to .md: %s\n' "$new_name"
done

prerequisites: A Linux terminal with bash 4 or newer
